title: After Making a Mistake
summary: Set a mistake down gently: regret and move on.
script:
Hi there. Welcome to this Meditation After Making a Mistake.
Wherever you are right now, however your day has gone, let yourself arrive here anyway. No need to feel a certain way before we begin.
Close your eyes, or keep them open and look softly in front of you.
Nothing to prepare for. Nothing to fix right this second. Just you, and a quiet few minutes.
Take a deep breath in.
And exhale, letting your shoulders drop a little as you do.
One more time. Breathe in and Breathe out.
I want you to bring something to mind. A mistake. Recent, maybe, or one that's been sitting with you for a while. Something you did, or said, or forgot to do, or that you wish had gone differently.
You don't need to relive every detail. Just let the general shape of it sit in your mind for a moment.
Breathe in slowly.
Notice how your body feels when you think about it. Maybe your stomach feels uncomfortable. Maybe you press your teeth together a little. This feeling is part of something called regret.
To regret something means you wish you had made a different choice or done something differently. Sometimes, you think about it again and again and you wish you could change what happened.
No need to push it away yet. Just see it clearly, the way you'd notice a weight you'd been carrying without realizing how heavy it had become.
Breathe out slowly.
Regret can come back again and again. It often comes when everything is quiet. Your mind may remember what happened and ask the same question: “What if I had done something differently?”

But notice something important. That moment is over. It already happened. The mistake is not happening now. What you have now is only the thought of it coming back to your mind. You are here, in this moment. You cannot change what already happened.
Breathe in.
Let's try something. Picture that mistake, whatever it was, as an object for a second. Maybe it's a stone, heavy, and rough, sitting in your hands.
You've been holding this stone for a while now. Maybe you've been looking at it again and again, thinking about every part of it.
Breathe out slowly.
Notice, you can set it down.
Not because the mistake didn't matter, not because you're pretending it didn't happen. Just because holding it any longer isn't changing what already happened. It’s only making your hands tired.
Breathe in, and as you do so, imagine your hands slowly opening and letting go of the stone.
Breathe out, and let the stone rest on the ground beside you, still there if you ever need to look at it again, but no longer something you have to carry constantly.
Notice your hands now, a little lighter.
Breathe in slowly.
This is what it means to move on. To move on doesn't mean forgetting, or pretending something didn't happen. It means you've let the weight of it settle down, so you can keep walking forward without carrying it in your hands the entire time. Think of it like closing a door gently behind you, not slamming it, not locking it, just closing it, so you can keep walking down the hallway ahead of you.
Breathe out completely.
Ask yourself, gently, what did this mistake teach you? Not to punish yourself with the answer, just to notice it. Maybe it taught you something about patience. Maybe about communication. Maybe simply that you're human, and humans get things wrong sometimes, without exception, everybody does.
Breathe in slowly.
Keep the lesson with you, like something small and useful in your pocket.
But leave the heavy stone behind. Let the regret stay there, on the ground, where you put it down. You can keep the lesson without carrying the regret.
Breathe out slowly.
You can look back at the stone anytime you want. It's still there. But you don't need to carry it with you all the time. You don't need to think about what happened again and again. Now, imagine walking a little farther down the hallway. Your hands are empty, and you feel a little lighter.
Breathe in.
Now, you can repeat these phrases out loud or just in your mind.
I made a mistake. That doesn't make me a mistake.
I am allowed to move on, even before I feel completely ready.
The moment already ended. I don't have to keep living inside it.
I am walking forward, lighter, with every breath.
Take one more slow breath in.
And breathe out, completely.
When you're ready to come back, start noticing small, real things around you. Whatever is supporting your body right now. Any sound nearby. Your breath, still slow, still yours.
Move your fingers first, gently. Then your feet.
Whenever it feels right, let your eyes open.
Carry this with you, into the rest of your day. Regret may still visit sometimes, quietly, that's alright, it's simply part of being human. But now you know, a little more clearly, how to set it down gently, and keep moving on, one step at a time.

vocabulary.definition: when you wish you had made a different choice or done something differently
to accept what happened and continue with your life instead of thinking about it again and again
